components.title: Volume keys
components.summary: A hold on the rocker ramps instead of stepping: our daemon prefers hhd's virtual volume keyboard, falls back to the free physical AT keyboard, degrades observably on EBUSY, and keeps a force-release hwdb as defence in depth.

install.summary: the standalone daemon (orchestrator --volume) or the hhd patch applied by oxp3-fixes.sh
steps: never combine the two: both normalise the same key

verify.expect: oxp3-voltap is active (running)
this boot's journal has grabbed /dev/input/eventN
the daemon would grab the hhd virtual volume keyboard, or a free physical fallback, and says why
the physical AT keyboard is held only by hhd (or by nobody); SKIP without root
the force-release entry exists and hwdb.bin is newer
a hold yields exactly one step, not a ramp

caveats: do not combine with the hhd volume patch from oxp3-fixes.sh install
the standing alternative is the hhd patch, which is why the doc says pick one
device discovery is by name/phys/capabilities plus /proc/*/fdinfo holders, never by eventN; exit 2 = no candidate, 3 = every grab refused

last_validated.evidence: tools/oxp3-voltap selftest and capture evidence in docs/hw/volume-buttons.md; not installed on the QA host (docs/QA.md row 34)

steps: or use the individual paths: --leds (home button), --rgb (keeper), --volume (rocker)

components.title: Suspend and wake policy
components.summary: Suspend works here (nine real s2idle cycles in the journal) but nothing in the current boots asks for it: logind had no Handle* policy (power-key default poweroff), KDE PowerDevil owns handle-*-key, and hhd only forwards the key to Steam in Gamepad mode; a shipped logind drop-in plus polkit rule make sleep reachable without a desktop session.

install.summary: three units, the wake-source rule, the logind/polkit trigger policy and the measurement tool

verify.expect: /sys/power/mem_sleep selects [s2idle]
oxp3-sleep-wakeup is active and reports the pre/log units
every listed USB id / PCI address has wakeup disabled
logind drop-in parsed with HandlePowerKey/SuspendKey=suspend, polkit rule present, pkcheck says yes, no sleep block inhibitor
the capability table and the suspend record block
success > 0 and last_hw_sleep > 0 (a real suspend)
PASS at or below 1 %/h, WARN 1-2 %/h, FAIL above 2 %/h
one real s2idle cycle (rtcwake) with suspend_stats/success incremented; needs --full --with-changes and OXP3_ALLOW_SUSPEND=1

caveats: sleep.suspend is the only check that really suspends the machine; it needs --full --with-changes and OXP3_ALLOW_SUSPEND=1
no real suspend recorded since install: run sudo tools/sleep-power-measure.sh suspend -w 600, or sudo systemctl suspend
sleep.measure SKIPs on AC by design
the logind drop-in is read at logind start: restart systemd-logind (or reboot) after installing
PowerDevil keeps owning handle-power-key while Plasma runs, so HandlePowerKey=suspend only takes effect when no desktop claims the key

last_validated.evidence: trigger audit: journalctl -b all -k shows 9x 'PM: suspend entry (s2idle)' (Oct 12-19) with the Oct 16 login1.Suspend call from Steam via xdg-dbus-proxy; systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/logind.conf = [Login] only (poweroff default); systemd-inhibit shows PowerDevil block on handle-*; pkcheck login1.suspend exit 0; hhd 4.1.12 plugins/powerbutton/base.py:30,89-106,311-338,341-371 quoted in docs/hw/sleep-power.md 2.5

components.title: Fan curve
components.summary: A manual PWM fan curve works through pwm1. The EC keeps no fan-curve table on this board (recovered 2026-11-09: its auto/manual, duty and tach registers are exactly what oxpec already drives), so userspace is the only place a curve can live.

install.summary: an opt-in unit installed inactive

verify.expect: fan1_input 1-12000 rpm and pwm1_enable 1 or 2
a curve file with duplicate temperature points is accepted (dry-run, one step)
the state file records mode=manual after pwm1_enable was written

caveats: SIGTERM restores EC auto mode
the acpi_fan EIO in the fan node is a known cosmetic bug
there is no vendor EC curve table to expose: Devs*FanCurve are ASUS WMI device ids; see upstream/oxpec-ec-addresses.md
the EC tach is 0x58/0x59 (upstream oxpec, OXP_2_SENSOR_FAN_REG); older notes said 0x76

last_validated.evidence: docs/QA.md row 44 (curve picks pwm 124 at 61 C in a dry run); docs/hw/power-fan.md EC findings

components.title: Battery care
components.summary: Charge limit and charge-inhibit ('bypass') are reachable through the driver's EC bytes, now identified: 0xA3 percent cap and 0xA4 bit mask (0x00/0x01/0x03). The charger tier (0xE3) and the charge floor (0xA5) have addresses but no ABI and no proven units.

install.summary: saved through the power tool after the power units are installed

verify.expect: a readable charge_control_end_threshold (80 when limited)
charge_behaviour lists inhibit-charge
no argument resolves to 100 % ('off') in a dry run and the real call is refused without root

caveats: the EC keeps the last saved limit until it is changed again
bypass is charge-inhibit (EC 0xA4), the same byte and values the vendor writes; whether the EC also isolates the pack from the rail is unproven
addresses: upstream/oxpec-ec-addresses.md; mode 1 (0x01) is awake-only, mode 2 (0x03) is always

last_validated.evidence: docs/QA.md row 44 (limit 80, behaviour auto on the QA host); docs/hw/battery-tdp.md
